DK26.4 is a specific medical diagnosis code used within the Danish healthcare system to identify a chronic or unspecified duodenal ulcer accompanied by hemorrhage (bleeding) [^src1]. It is one of the many standardized ICD-10-DK codes utilized by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to track clinical outcomes and measure the quality of care for patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] [^src1]. 

Specifically, DK26.4 is included in a comprehensive set of diagnostic codes used to calculate the incidence of severe bleeding events among the atrial fibrillation patient population [^src1]. This indicator is crucial for monitoring the safety of treatments, such as anticoagulant therapy, which carries a known risk of gastrointestinal and other severe bleeding complications. The code is grouped alongside other gastrointestinal bleeding codes (such as [[dk25-0|DK25.0]] through [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]] and [[dk92-0|DK92.0]] through [[dk92-2|DK92.2]]), intracranial bleeding codes (like [[di60|DI60]] to [[ds066|DS066]]), and respiratory/urinary tract bleeding codes (such as [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]]) to form a broad safety net for capturing adverse bleeding events in national clinical quality databases [^src1]. 

The definition and application of DK26.4 are formally documented in the annual reports for the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database, serving as a technical reference for standardized data collection and regional comparison across the Danish healthcare system in both 2023 and 2024 [^src2].
